Read receiver deployments from an OTN, GLATOS or detqc sheet

Source: R/read_deployments.R
read_deployments.Rd

Reads a deployment file into a data frame with the contract's deployment columns. It reads CSV files and the sheet of an Excel workbook whose header names the most mapped columns; the header row is found by its names, so title rows above it are skipped. Mapped: OTN deployment sheets (the instrument deployment short form), OTN deployment CSV files, OTN AAT receiver files, the OTN moorings receivers file (receiver serial in rcvrserial), the OTN stations-receivers file (rcvr_serial), GLATOS receiver location files and the deployment sheet of a GLATOS project workbook. Excel needs the readxl package.

Usage

read_deployments(
  file,
  format = c("auto", "otn", "glatos", "detqc"),
  col_map = NULL,
  tz = NULL
)

Arguments

file

Path to a CSV or Excel file.

format

One of "auto", "otn", "glatos" or "detqc".

col_map

Optional column map. A data frame, or the path to a CSV file, laid out as column_map() describes, replaces the packaged map. Pairs written as c(target = "source") are merged into the format's map: each replaces the rows of its target, and the other targets are read as the format reads them. A pair whose column is not in the file stops; column_map() gives the order in which a pair names the columns the format joins, as GLATOS joins two for transmitter.

tz

Optional time zone, from OlsonNames(), for stamps that carry no zone of their own. NULL uses the zone in the column map (UTC for every packaged format).

Value

A data frame with receiver_serial, station_id, deploy_datetime, recover_datetime (UTC; NA while deployed), deploy_lat, deploy_lon, deploy_z, receiver_transmitter where the sheet has it, recovery_status and any other columns. The attribute source records the file, the map rows used and the rows dropped for want of a deployment time.

Details

Format. "auto" reads the file with the map, OTN or GLATOS, that fills more of the contract columns from the file's columns, and OTN on a tie. When the other format's map would fill a contract column that the chosen one leaves empty, such as deploy_z, a warning names the column and the format. Where that column is one the table needs, such as station_id of a GLATOS receiver file read with format = "otn", the reader stops and names the format "auto" picks. A format other than the four stops with the formats listed. A file with detqc's own column names, such as a detset's deployments written with write.csv(), fills the most contract columns and is read as "detqc". A blank-headed first column of unique whole numbers, the row names write.csv() writes by default, is dropped.

A GLATOS workbook keeps its recoveries on its Recovery sheet, which is joined to the deployments as glatos::read_glatos_workbook() joins it, and its times in local time, in glatos_deploy_date_time and glatos_recover_date_time at the zone in glatos_timezone; where the UTC columns are blank, these are converted to UTC. The attribute source counts both, in recoveries_joined and local_times.

A sheet that records no receiver serial, as OTN's deployment CSV does, gives receiver_serial as NA; detset() then matches detections to those deployments by station_id, and audit_listening() keys their days by station. A moorings or stations-receivers file with the serial blank on some rows is read the same way on those rows. An OTN deployment CSV names its station in STATION_NAME, or in STATION_NO beside ARRAY, which is read alone. A workbook's OTN_ARRAY and STATION_NO are joined. OTN projects differ in which of the two their detections use, so a project named the other way gives col_map = c(station_id = "station_no") for a workbook or col_map = c(station_id = "array;station_no") for a CSV. A file from which the map fills no station_id in any row is read with a warning that names the columns the map looked for.

A file with no column the map reads for recover_datetime, and no recovery in any row, is read with a warning that names the columns the map looked for, since every deployment then reads as never recovered. A recovery column that is blank in every row gives no warning: its receivers are still deployed.

Rows with no deployment time are dropped with a warning that counts them and names their stations; detset() logs the count. Rows whose receiver_model names an instrument that is not a receiver, such as the "anchor" rows of an OTN short form, and that carry no receiver serial, are not deployments: they are set aside with a message and counted in dropped_not_receiver. A recovery date written with a status, such as "failed: 2010-03-07" or "caught: 2014-06-22", keeps its date, and the text goes to recovery_status; a warning counts these rows. A recovery with no date, such as "failed", is read from the next mapped column (last_download in OTN sheets) or left NA.

A station is one fixed place. A warning counts the station_id values whose deployments lie more than 1 km apart, as GLATOS station codes that repeat across projects do, and the attribute source keeps the count (stations_over_1km).

The receiver's own transmitter. The TRANSMITTER column of an OTN instrument deployment short form holds, for a transceiver, the pinger built into the receiver, and otherwise a sentinel tag on the same mooring. It is read as receiver_transmitter, in capitals with the ends trimmed. A value that is not a transmitter id (code space and ID, as "A69-1601-12345"), such as a bare number, becomes NA with a warning that counts such rows, and the attribute source keeps the count (receiver_transmitter_malformed). check_detset() and audit_listening() take these ids as the reference tags when you give none. The GLATOS receiver and workbook layouts mapped here have no such column.

Times in OTN and GLATOS sheets are UTC. A sheet kept in local time is read with tz, and an Excel date-time number is read in the same zone.

See also

column_map() to read a sheet with other column names.

Examples

receivers_file <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_receivers.csv", package = "detqc")
deployments <- read_deployments(receivers_file)
attr(deployments, "source")$format
#> [1] "glatos"
head(deployments)
#>   receiver_serial station_id     deploy_datetime    recover_datetime

#> 2            R002       S002 2024-06-01 14:00:00 2024-06-11 15:00:00

#>   deploy_lat deploy_lon deploy_z receiver_model consecutive_deploy_no

#> 2   44.50416  -78.19781     9.13          VR2Tx                     1

# An OTN short form whose TRANSMITTER column holds each receiver's own
# transmitter; R020's id has no code space and is read as NA
otn_file <- system.file("extdata", "stoney_otn_deployments.csv", package = "detqc")
otn_deployments <- read_deployments(otn_file, format = "otn")
#> Warning: stoney_otn_deployments.csv: 1 receiver_transmitter value is not a transmitter id (code space and ID, as "A69-1601-12345"), such as "60020"; it was read as NA, and no reference tag is taken from it.
tail(otn_deployments[, c("receiver_serial", "receiver_transmitter")], 3)
#>    receiver_serial receiver_transmitter
#> 18            R018       A69-1601-60018
#> 19            R019       A69-1601-60019
#> 20            R020                 <NA>
